title: How to Get a Taxi in China With No Chinese — DiDi | China Travel Expert
description:
In China you barely ever hail a cab on the street — you tap a screen. Here's the taxi trick every first-timer needs.

The app is DiDi, China's dominant ride-hailing service (550M+ users across 400+ cities). It has a full English version, but in 2026 the smoothest setup for tourists is opening DiDi as a mini-program inside Alipay — it's more stable, translates better, and lets you pay with a linked foreign Visa or Mastercard. Type your destination (or just drop a pin), pick DiDi Express for the cheapest ride, and the app shows your driver's name, plate and ETA up front. Two gotchas: at airports, train stations and big malls you must walk to a marked "designated zone" (green dots on the map) for pickup, and your driver will ask for the last four digits of your phone number to confirm it's you.

🧭 Expert Tip: Install DiDi (or the Alipay mini-program) and verify your card on home Wi-Fi before you fly — doing it on airport Wi-Fi is slow and painful.
